title: Bank Deposit On-Time Promise: Late-Delivery Refund of the Transfer Fee
content:
On a Bank Deposit tier that carries the on-time promise, a transfer deposited after its date of availability is owed a late-delivery refund on its transfer fee, booked as one refund against the transfer-fee charge with the reason late delivery, and the amount refunded is the late-delivery refund for that transfer rather than the whole transfer fee.

## Whose lateness it is

Lateness is the customer's, and no late-delivery refund is owed, only when a payout on the transfer came back for a reason attributed to the sender or when the transfer was held for a request for information whose answer was logged after the answer window; a hold Paloma placed for its own screening or review is never the customer's lateness, and neither is a deposit made to account details the customer supplied when no payout came back.

| What the transfer's records show (promise tier, deposited after the date of availability) | Lateness is the customer's? | Late-delivery refund owed? |
|---|---|---|
| A payout came back for a reason attributed to the sender | yes | no |
| Held for a request for information, answer logged after the answer window | yes | no |
| Held only for Paloma's own screening or review | no | yes |
| Deposited to account details the customer supplied, no payout came back | no | yes |
| None of the situations above | no | yes |

## What the refund books

One late-delivery refund is booked on the transfer's ledger as a fee refund with the reason late delivery against the transfer-fee charge, dated the day it is booked. The money goes back to the customer's original payment method, the refund then shows on the transfer's money movements, and the fees Paloma holds on the transfer fall by the amount refunded.

## Booking it: `refund_late_delivery_fee_f06ff624`

**Owner and invocation.** This is an agent-side tool. The agent unlocks `refund_late_delivery_fee_f06ff624` and then calls it. Each call books one fee refund with the reason late delivery.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `bank_transfer_id` | The reference number of the Bank Deposit transfer whose transfer fee is being refunded, as returned by the Bank Deposit transfer lookup for this customer | identifier |
| `related_entry_id` | The reference number of the money movement that charged the transfer fee being refunded, as returned by the Bank Deposit money-movement lookup for that transfer | identifier |
| `refund_amount_usd` | The amount of the transfer fee refunded, in US dollars | positive number with 2 decimal places (cents); recorded exactly as passed after rounding half up to 2 decimal places |

**Return.** A dictionary rendered as text with `ledger_entry_id` (the reference number of the new fee refund movement), `bank_transfer_id` (the transfer refunded), `refunded_usd` (the amount refunded, US dollars with 2 decimal places), `fee_refund_reason` (always `late_delivery`), `entry_date` (the refund date, YYYY-MM-DD), `fees_held_usd` (the fees Paloma still holds on the transfer afterwards, US dollars with 2 decimal places) and `status` (refunded when the refund was booked).

## Points of judgement

- **A Bank Deposit transfer held by Paloma's own compliance screening and deposited late.** That hold is never the customer's lateness, so the refund is owed.
- **A late transfer one of whose payouts came back for a reason attributed to the sender.** The lateness is the customer's, so no late-delivery refund is owed, even though the transfer was later deposited.
- **A transfer deposited on its date of availability.** It was not deposited after that date, so no late-delivery refund arises.
